fieldValues.comment_text: Challenger: The framing says there are "two models", but there are more like five copies, and they have already drifted apart. srs-programme installs both method and argument. Its argument package has the same IDs as muSrs's, yet its blueprints and compositions differ. /home/greenman/dev/semanticops/clerk/packages/method is a second copy of method whose types and relations differ from srs-programme's, for example persona-in-domain and holds-domain. So "practise side by side" is not a controlled experiment. It is uncontrolled forking, and the owner's own comment, "many versions of this wheel", says as much. Question 4 also assumes the essay package has some linking to decide. It barely has any: /home/greenman/dev/muDemocracy.org/muSrs/packages/essay/relation-types holds three relations (bears-on, counters, comments-on), and only bears-on targets a chain type: paragraph to argument problem. Problem is the only type both chains share, and the owner calls everything after it "unformed". Choosing between method, argument or a shared core now would build on that unformed part. The 24 October domain ratification also forbids treating a muSrs problem as a programme problem. Owner: should the next action be one essay, in one repository, that links its paragraphs only to problems, and nothing past problem until that hurts?
